messages:
Maya (CEO): kicking off a short follow-up for partnership & GTM questions from today's all-hands. ask specific trade-offs (co-sell, marketplace, pricing) and we'll reply.
Noah - Head of Product: quick clarifier  do we want a Redwood marketplace for third-party models/apps, or keep catalog curated?
Lina (Strategy): strategic pick: curated catalog now; marketplace later after we have clear security + billing primitives. curated helps control quality and latency expectations.
Priya (Head of Sales): practical tension: some enterprise buyers want vendor bundles (SI + infra). are we open to revenue share channel partners?
Maya (CEO): yes to selective revenue share with system integrators and MSPs for regulated verticals. not a broad affiliate program yet. prioritize partners with compliance reach.
Jules (DevEx): developer story question: if we enable marketplace listings, how do we keep the "developer-first" promise (easy to test, predictable latency)?
Noah - Head of Product: marketplace entries must pass a performance & perf-cost audit before listing. default to sandboxed runtimes and clear latency badges.
Sasha (Research): data note: partners that co-sell reduced enterprise sales cycles by ~20% in our pilot. will share anonymized numbers.
Priya (Head of Sales): pricing models  should Sales push committed capacity (Dedicated) or pay-as-you-go hosted for early-stage customers? guidance for qualification?
Lina (Strategy): rule of thumb: self-serve hosted for early-stage/prod trials; committed Dedicated when predictable throughput or compliance is required. highlight unit economics for both.
Maya (CEO): add nuance: for buyers that care about predictable ops costs, lead with Dedicated. for builder-first teams, lead with hosted + Optimize to reduce spend.
Jules (DevEx): docs ask: can we publish a short "which product fits me" flowchart for onboarding? would reduce handoffs.
Noah - Head of Product: yes  Product + DevEx to ship a one-page flowchart and sample configs. target EOD Friday.
Priya (Head of Sales): competitor messaging: how blunt should SDRs be about large cloud providers? avoid name-calling but need fast rebuttal.
Maya (CEO): SDR script: "Cloud providers give model access; Redwood delivers production guarantees, cost controls, and deployment choices." keep tone comparative, not combative.
Sasha (Research): also share two short benchmark cards: one latency-focused, one cost-focused, plus a quick case of a regulated customer using Private.
Lina (Strategy): question on co-marketing: do we allow partner logos on our site? protects trust but might complicate partner relations.
Maya (CEO): allow selective co-marketing with signed MOU; legal to confirm approved logos. prioritize partners with clear customer references.
Jules (DevEx): integration note: if partners ship model adapters, how do we handle support boundaries? who triages model bugs vs infra issues?
Noah - Head of Product: define SLOs for partner integrations and a joint-support playbook. buyers deserve a single escalation path.
Priya (Head of Sales): ask about incentives: will we offer referral credits or discounting for partner-driven deals?
Maya (CEO): yes for initial pilots: referral credits and a structured discount tier for MSP/Systems Integrator partners. Finance to detail terms.
Sasha (Research): one last ask  what are the three metrics leadership will watch to evaluate partner strategy success?
Maya (CEO): good call: 1) partner-sourced ARR, 2) average sales cycle length for partner deals vs direct, 3) customer NPS for partner-supported accounts.
Noah - Head of Product: we'll draft a short partner playbook and an internal FAQ. DevEx/Marketing to review.
partners-bot: partner-pilot: created entry "SI co-sell pilot" assigned to Priya; doc link: https://redwood.example/partners/si-pilot
Maya (CEO): thanks all  please keep follow-ups concise. owners: Priya (pilot), Noah (playbook), Jules (flowchart), Sasha (benchmarks). closing thread. :rocket:
